title: Downloading, Saving, and Printing Web Content
description: Practice downloading files, saving web pages, and printing content from the browser
objective: Students will download files from the internet, save web pages in multiple formats, print web content as PDF, manage the download manager, and practice essential keyboard shortcuts

steps.title: Download and Manage Files
steps.instructions:
Let us practice downloading files from the internet and managing them.

**Step A: Download a PDF file**
1. Open Google and search for: `CCC exam syllabus filetype:pdf`
2. Click on a PDF result to open it in Chrome
3. Click the **Download** icon (down arrow) in the PDF viewer
4. Save it to your **Desktop** with the name: `CCC_Syllabus.pdf`

**Step B: Open Download Manager**
1. Press **Ctrl + J** to open the Downloads page
2. You should see the file you just downloaded
3. Click **Show in folder** to open the folder where the file was saved
4. Verify the file is on your Desktop

**Step C: Download an image**
1. Go to https://www.google.com
2. Right-click on the Google logo
3. Click **Save image as...**
4. Save to your Desktop as `google_logo.png`
5. Check Ctrl + J again — the image should appear in downloads

**Step D: Check your Downloads folder**
1. Open File Explorer (Windows + E)
2. Navigate to: `C:\Users\YourName\Downloads`
3. How many files are in this folder? _______________
4. List 3 different file types you see:
   - _______________
   - _______________
   - _______________

**Step E: Change download location (optional)**
1. In Chrome, go to Settings > Downloads
2. Note the current download path: _______________
3. You can click **Change** to set a different folder

**Questions:**
- What is the shortcut to open Download Manager? _______________
- What is the default download folder on Windows? _______________
- Why should you be careful downloading .exe files? _______________

steps.title: Save Web Pages in Multiple Formats
steps.instructions:
Sometimes you need to save a web page to read offline. There are several ways to do this.

**Method 1: Save as HTML (Ctrl + S)**
1. Open: https://www.nielit.gov.in
2. Press **Ctrl + S**
3. In the Save dialog:
   - Location: Desktop
   - File name: `NIELIT_Page`
   - Save as type: **Webpage, Complete**
4. Click Save
5. Go to your Desktop — you should see:
   - A file: `NIELIT_Page.html`
   - A folder: `NIELIT_Page_files` (contains images, CSS, etc.)
6. Double-click the HTML file — it opens in your browser with all images!

**Method 2: Save as PDF (Ctrl + P > Save as PDF)**
1. Open: https://www.irctc.co.in
2. Press **Ctrl + P** to open Print dialog
3. Change **Destination** to: **Save as PDF**
4. Set Layout to: **Portrait**
5. Click **Save**
6. Save to Desktop as: `IRCTC_Page.pdf`
7. Open the PDF — it looks like a printed version of the website!

**Method 3: Save as Single File (MHTML)**
1. Open any web page
2. Press **Ctrl + S**
3. Change Save as type to: **Webpage, Single File**
4. Save to Desktop as: `SingleFile_Test.mhtml`
5. This saves everything in ONE file (no separate folder)

**Compare the three methods:**
| Method | Files Created | Size | Offline Images? |
|--------|--------------|------|----------------|
| HTML Complete | File + Folder | Large | Yes |
| PDF | One PDF file | Medium | Yes (as snapshot) |
| Single File | One MHTML file | Medium | Yes |

**Real-life usage:** Amit needs to save his IRCTC train ticket. Which method should he use? _______________
Answer: Save as PDF — it is the most portable and accepted format for tickets and documents.

steps.title: Print Web Content
steps.instructions:
Printing web pages is an important skill — from admit cards to train tickets. Let us practice.

**Step A: Open Print Dialog**
1. Open any web page with content (e.g., a news article from timesofindia.com or ndtv.com)
2. Press **Ctrl + P** to open Print dialog
3. Explore the print options on the left side:
   - **Destination:** Your printer name or "Save as PDF"
   - **Pages:** All, or specify page numbers (e.g., 1-2)
   - **Layout:** Portrait (tall) or Landscape (wide)
   - **Color:** Color or Black and White

**Step B: Practice Print Settings**
With the print dialog open:
1. Change Layout to **Landscape** — notice how the preview changes
2. Change it back to **Portrait**
3. Click **More settings** to expand additional options
4. Try changing:
   - Paper size: **A4** (standard in India)
   - Margins: **Minimum** (notice more content fits on the page)
   - Scale: **80%** (notice the text becomes smaller but more fits on each page)
   - Headers and footers: Turn off (removes URL and date from printout)

**Step C: Save a news article as PDF**
1. With the print dialog still open
2. Set Destination to **Save as PDF**
3. Set Layout to **Portrait**, Paper to **A4**
4. Click **Save**
5. Save to Desktop as: `News_Article.pdf`
6. Open the PDF to verify it looks correct

**Step D: Print only selected text**
1. Close the print dialog (press Escape)
2. On the web page, select (click and drag) just 2-3 paragraphs of text
3. Press **Ctrl + P** again
4. In the Pages option, look for **Selection only** option
5. Only your selected text should appear in the preview
6. Save as PDF to see the result

**Questions:**
- What is the shortcut to open Print dialog? _______________
- What paper size is standard in India? _______________
- How do you save a web page as PDF without a printer? _______________

steps.title: Copy Text and Images from Websites
steps.instructions:
Learn to copy content from websites and paste it into documents.

**Step A: Copy text**
1. Open: https://www.nielit.gov.in
2. Find a paragraph of text on the page
3. Click at the beginning of the text
4. Hold the mouse button and drag to select 2-3 lines (text turns blue)
5. Press **Ctrl + C** to copy
6. Open **Notepad** (search in Start menu)
7. Press **Ctrl + V** to paste
8. The text should appear in Notepad!

**Step B: Copy an image**
1. Go to https://www.google.com
2. Right-click on the Google logo
3. Click **Copy image**
4. Open **Paint** (search in Start menu)
5. Press **Ctrl + V** to paste the image
6. The Google logo should appear in Paint!
7. Save it: File > Save As > PNG > Desktop > `copied_logo.png`

**Step C: Select all content**
1. Open any web page
2. Press **Ctrl + A** to select ALL content on the page
3. Notice everything gets highlighted
4. Press **Ctrl + C** to copy everything
5. Open a Word document or Notepad
6. Press **Ctrl + V** to paste
7. All the text (and sometimes images) from the page are pasted!

**Step D: Use Find on Page**
1. Open any web page with lots of text
2. Press **Ctrl + F** to open the Find bar
3. Type a word you want to find (e.g., "computer")
4. The browser highlights all matching words on the page
5. Use the up/down arrows in the Find bar to jump between matches
6. How many matches were found? _______________
7. Press **Escape** to close the Find bar

**Step E: Zoom practice**
1. On any web page:
   - Press **Ctrl + +** (plus) three times — text gets bigger
   - What is the zoom level? _______________% (check in the address bar area)
   - Press **Ctrl + -** (minus) three times — text gets smaller
   - Press **Ctrl + 0** (zero) — resets to 100%

**Summary of shortcuts practiced:**
| Action | Shortcut |
|--------|----------|
| Copy | Ctrl + C |
| Paste | Ctrl + V |
| Select All | Ctrl + A |
| Find on Page | Ctrl + F |
| Zoom In | Ctrl + + |
| Zoom Out | Ctrl + - |
| Reset Zoom | Ctrl + 0 |

steps.title: Keyboard Shortcut Challenge
steps.instructions:
Let us test how many keyboard shortcuts you have learned. Complete each challenge without using the mouse!

**Challenge 1: Tab Management (no mouse!)**
1. Press **Ctrl + T** to open a new tab
2. Type `google.com` and press Enter
3. Press **Ctrl + T** again for another new tab
4. Type `irctc.co.in` and press Enter
5. Press **Ctrl + T** for a third tab
6. Type `digilocker.gov.in` and press Enter
7. Press **Ctrl + Tab** to switch to the next tab
8. Press **Ctrl + Shift + Tab** to switch to the previous tab
9. Press **Ctrl + W** to close the current tab
10. Press **Ctrl + Shift + T** to reopen the closed tab
Did it reopen? _______________

**Challenge 2: Page Actions (no mouse!)**
1. On any web page, press **F5** to refresh
2. Press **Ctrl + D** to add a bookmark — press Enter to save
3. Press **Ctrl + H** to open history — take note of recent items
4. Press **Ctrl + J** to open downloads
5. Press **Ctrl + P** to open print dialog — press Escape to cancel
6. Press **Ctrl + F** to open Find — type any word — press Escape
7. Press **F11** to enter full screen
8. Press **F11** again to exit full screen

**Challenge 3: Shortcut Quiz**
Write the shortcut for each action WITHOUT looking at your notes:

| Action | Your Answer | Correct Answer |
|--------|------------|----------------|
| New tab | | Ctrl + T |
| Close tab | | Ctrl + W |
| Bookmark page | | Ctrl + D |
| Print page | | Ctrl + P |
| Save page | | Ctrl + S |
| Open history | | Ctrl + H |
| Open downloads | | Ctrl + J |
| Find on page | | Ctrl + F |
| Incognito mode | | Ctrl + Shift + N |
| Refresh page | | F5 |
| Full screen | | F11 |
| Zoom in | | Ctrl + + |
| Zoom out | | Ctrl + - |
| Clear browsing data | | Ctrl + Shift + Del |
| Reopen closed tab | | Ctrl + Shift + T |

How many did you get correct? ___ / 15

**Score Guide:**
- 13-15: Excellent! You are ready for the CCC exam shortcuts.
- 10-12: Good! Review the ones you missed.
- Below 10: Practice more — these shortcuts are frequently asked in the exam.

**Submit your completed shortcut quiz table with your lab report.**
